chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his father, from 'Amru ibn Jumay', who raised it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:
The price of Paradise is 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god except Allah).

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ ص: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the abode of eternal bliss
key_terms.ثَمَنُ: Price, cost, or means of acquisition
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The declaration of monotheism (Shahadah), meaning 'There is no god except Allah'

ai.seo_question: What is the price of Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) metaphorically identifies the declaration of monotheism, 'La ilaha illallah', as the 'price' (thaman) of Paradise, highlighting it as the essential currency for spiritual acquisition. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that while faith is the foundation, the active verbal affirmation and internalization of Tawhid serve as the decisive means to attain the ultimate reward. It connects the theological concept of divine unity directly to the eschatological outcome, reinforcing the centrality of the Shahada in Islamic soteriology.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. And from the previous chain from al-Hussain b. Sayf from his father from ’Amru b. Jamee’ who raised it to The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) who said:
The price of Paradise is Laa ilaaha illallaah (there is no God except Allah).
